observer.why_cursor: The 'until' above is a CLAUDE-CODE fact: that script captures tool outcomes and the jawata-fallback audit trail, so cutting it over would lose them. CURSOR's observer script loses nothing, because it does nothing — its whole body is `cat > /dev/null` then `printf '{}'`, and the role's Cursor row in roles.rs declares query, record and emit all false. Two generations that both do nothing are not a parity question. It stays REGISTERED rather than dropped because afterMCPExecution is Cursor's only post-tool injection point, so this entry is the seam the outcome-capture work will arrive through. Windows forced it: a .sh cannot execute there, and Cursor firing one on every tool call put a window on the user's screen every time — a no-op that costs nothing and interrupts constantly.
